2. The present application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, has been instituted praying for grant of regular bail to the accused petitioner, Shri Abani Mudoi @
Aboni, who was arrested on 17.09.2025 and is presently languishing in judicial custody, in connection with Garamur P.S. Case No. 42/2025 registered under Sections 123/274/275 of BNS,
2023 (corresponding to G.R. No. 82/2025).

sentences.text: the accused petitioner for observing the 829 th Death Anniversary of Sri Sri Madhabdev at Goalgaon Hari Mandir, for use as Prasad at the said Namghar.

It is further alleged that on eating the Prasad,
the villagers of Goalgaon suffered from stomach pain, fever, headache, vomiting and they were admitted to Sri Sri Pitambar Dev C.H.C., Garmur.
It is alleged that the accused petitioner had stored the lentils by sprinkling poison over it.
4. Police on receipt of the said FIR had registered the same as Garamur P.S. Case No. 42/2025 under Sections 123/274/275 of BNS, 2023.

5. Mr. S P Sharma, learned counsel for the accused petitioner submits that the allegation as leveled against the petitioner of having stored the moong dal (lentils) by sprinkling poison over it, is not sustainable in view of the report of the Food Analyst of the said moong dal (lentils), sample of which was forwarded to the said authority.

6. Mr. Sharma, learned counsel for the accused petitioner has relied upon the report of the Food Analyst dated 26.09.2025, wherein, it has been opined that the sample of moong dal (lentils) as forwarded conforms to be prescribed standards as laid down in Regulation 2.3.1 of the Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins & Residues) Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins & Residues) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
7. Mr. Sharma has further relied on the report of the Rectal swab of the victims, which was analysed by the Associate Professor, Department of Microbiology, Jorhat Medical College & Hospital, Jorhat,
which reveals that the victims had suffered ailments on account of Enteropathogenic Escherichia Coli (EPEC) infection.

He submits that the report of the Food Analyst as well as that of the Rectal swab analysis do not reveal that the ailments suffered by the victims were on account of any organo-phosphate or chemical poisoning, but was on account of bacterial contamination.
He also submits that the said report does not implicate the petitioner, herein, with regard to the allegation leveled against him under Sections 123/274/275 of BNSS, 2023.

In the above premises, Mr. Sharma,
learned counsel for the petitioner, herein, prays that the accused petitioner be enlarged on regular bail.
Page No.# 3/4 8.

Mr. K K Parashar, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, Assam submits that the allegation leveled against the accused petitioner is serious and the lentils as procured from the accused petitioner on being consumed having affected a large number of people, this Court at this stage would be pleased not to enlarge the accused petitioner on bail.
9. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and also perused the materials available on record.

10. The primary allegation leveled against the accused petitioner, herein, is that the moong dal (lentils) as procured from him on being consumed as Prasad by the villagers of Goalgaon village,
they had suffered ailments and it was suspected that the same was on account of the fact that the lentils were sold by the accused petitioner after mixing the same with poison.

The report of the Food Analyst reveals that the sample of the lentils as forwarded,
conforms to the standards laid down in Regulation 2.3.1 of the Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins & Residues) Regulations, 2011.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Further, the report of the Rectal swab of the victims reveals that they had suffered ailments on account of infection caused by Enteropathogenic Escherichia Coli (EPEC).
11.
Considering the said report, this Court is of the prima-facie view that further custodial interrogation of the accused petitioner, herein, may not be called for.
Accordingly, the accused petitioner is entitled to be enlarged on regular bail.
Any violation of the above condition would be good ground for the respondents to initiate the process for cancellation of the liberty of bail granted by this Court to the petitioner, herein.
14. With the above observations and directions, this bail application stands disposed of.
